Commentary.Commentary: The Indian top order just did not get going, Kohli and Rohit got off to starts but none went onto make it into something significant. Had it not been for Axar and Ashwin, India would have conceded a big lead to the Aussies. Now this game has become a one-innings shoutout. There are still around overs to go and India will hope they can get a couple at least. Australia on the other hand, will hope they can get through this passage without a lot of damage. An important phase follows.

Before that, it was the Nathan Lyon show on Day 2. He ran through the Indian top order. He was well supported by Todd Murphy and Matthew Kuhnemann. However, they had no answers to the counter-attack by Axar Patel and Ravichandran Ashwin but the second new ball worked really well for them. They have got a lead but it is of just the one run.

So, Australia just manage the lead of 1 run! That is an excellent recovery from the Indians. Australia on the other hand, will be very disappointed. Let me remind you, India were 7 down for 139 but then came a brilliant stand between Axar Patel and Ravichandran Ashwin! The two added over 100 and took India close to Australia's score. Axar Patel was the mainstay and Ashwin played second fiddle. In the end, that stand has changed the look of the game completely.

... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Another good session for the Aussies but India fought back well at the end of it courtesy Axar Patel and Ravichandran Ashwin! The session began with Jadeja and Kohli looking to get India back on safer shores but the former fell. The latter then followed and Srikar Bharat also did not last for long in the middle. Yet again it was the Aussie spinners who weaved their magic. Nathan Lyon got Srikar Bharat to get his fifer. India were in a lot of trouble with the trail being over 100 and the hosts were 7 down. Axar Patel though has come out all guns blazing and has scored quickly to put a little bit of pressure back on Australia and Ashwin has given him able support. The two need to continue the good work though. Australia on the other hand, will know one wicket and they'll be into the tail. They would be aiming for a lead of over 50. Can they get it?

That is a top session for the Aussies and one can say, they are on top in this game at the moment. They have bagged four wickets and not let India score freely too. However, it was India who began the day on the brighter note as Rahul and Rohit seemed at ease but after the introduction of Lyon, things changed, he has all four of the wickets and is looking really threatening. Jadeja and Kohli have started off well and are fighting back but the two need to continue as INdia are still 175 runs behind. Australia on the other hand, need to continue to be patient and disciplined with their lines and lengths. The second session could be a vital one, do join us in a bit.

Everything happening here! Australia now take another review as an appeal for an LBW is turned down. The question is, is it pad first or bat first? If it is pad first, it could be a good review. Here we go... ULTRA EDGE CONFIRMS IT IS PAD FIRST! OUT! BALL TRACKER SHOWS THREE REDS! Nathan Lyon is on fire and Cheteshwar Pujara falls for a duck on his 100th Test. All of a sudden, India are three down. This is tossed up on middle, it lands and turns back in. Pujara looks to defend but does so outside the line. It hits both bat and pad. A huge shout but not given. Australia finally manage to get a review right. India still trail by another 209 runs.
Virat Kohli is off the mark! A little too full and on middle, this is whipped down to long on for one.

DRINKS! Those two wickets by Lyon has got the Aussies back into the game. Before that, the Indian openers were going along really well but Lyon is amidst a really good spell. He could have easily had three had the review been taken against Pujara. India now need a partnership but the wicket is getting tougher to bat on. Interesting phase coming up.

OUT! TIMBER! Nathan Lyon now has both the openers! Two early wickets for the Aussies this morning and it is of the Indian skipper who was looking really good. Rohit Sharma just did not read the length there. This is flatter, it lands on middle and then skids through. Rohit goes back to a ball he should have probably been ahead too. The ball sneaks through before the bat comes down as he tries to flick and then hits the stumps. Australia back in the contest now.

A loud shout but not given! Maybe Pujara coming down the track saved him there. This is tossed up on off and it turns back in. Cheteshwar Pujara looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. A long disucssion between the Aussie players but no review taken. GUESS WHAT? Hawk Eye shows three reds! Australia probably did not take that as they had only one review left. A big opportunity goes abegging.
Tossed up on off, blocked.

ANOTHER REVIEW! This time it is taken by Rahul who has been given out lBW> He reviewed immediately. IS THERE AN INSIDE EDGE? Nothing on Ultra Edge. It seems like Australia have got their first wicket. OUT! They indeed have as it is clipping the leg pole. That is all they needed. Nathan Lyon strikes and that is a welcome wicket for the Aussies. Rahul walks bak for another low score. This lands around off and then spins in sharply. Rahul looks to defend but misses to get hit on the pads. He does not play for the turn. An appeal and the finger is raised immediately. India do not lose a review but their first wicket. The hosts still trail by 3 short of 220.

Another review! This time for a catch! Has it taken the inside edge before hitting the pad? Rahul looks quite calm about it. Well the catch is out of question as it is a mile away from the bat. Seems like Australia might just lose another review. THEY DO! NOT OUT! It is going over when checked for the LBW. Desperate stuff from the Aussies. This lands outside off and then jags back in. Rahul looks to defend but misses. It hits the pad and lobs to the slip fielder. An appeal but turned down. Australia now have lost two reviews.
Good delivery! This one lands outside off and then jags back in. Rahul looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

SIX! That is a top shot! Rahul uses his feet, gets to the pitch of it and then tonks it over the lone on fence for a biggie. Got close to the pitch of the ball and took the spin out of question.
Better line! On off, Rahul defends.

A huge appeal but turned down! Carey seemed very interested and Cummins take the review. Seems to be going down leg. Judging by the first replay, that seems a poor review. NOT OUT! That is a poor a review. The impact is umpire's call and it is also missing leg. Australia lose a review. Angled into the pads. Rahul looks to defend but misses to get hit on the pads. That just went on with the angle and did not straighten.
Another single as this is eased down to long off.

First run of the day! Length and on off, Rahul waits and then guides it towards point for one.
BEATEN! Actually he played that well in the end. It is on a length and around off, it lands and moves away. Rahul pulls his bat back after seeing the movement.
Right on the money to begin with! On a length and around off, blocked.

That is a lovely ball to end a testing first over of the day. The last two balls are probably the pace one wants to bowl on this surface. Yet again, looped up a little. It lands on off and then spins away. Rohit lunges to defend but is beaten by the turn. Yet again, encouraging signs for India.
Well bowled! Slows it up this time, gives it a little bit more air, it lands on off and turns away slightly, Rohit looks to defend but it goes off the outer half towards the off side.
Angled into the pads this time, Rohit works it to mid-wicket.
On the quicker side this time and on off, Rohit pushes it to mid off.
Slightly fuller this time and on off, Rohit pushes it to mid off.
Starts off well, tosses it up on off, gets it to drift in and then turn away after landing, just a little. Defended.
We are all set to begin! The Indian openers, KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma walk out and so do the Aussie players. Spin to begin with as it is Matthew Kuhnemann!
UPDATE - Australia have a concussion substitue, David Warner who took a few blows on the head while batting has been ruled out of the Test with concussion and it is Matt Renshaw who replaces him.

The Aussies on the other hand, need to strike at regular intervals. There were encouraging sings fir their bowlers in the last session but can they make use of the assistance? Can the Australian bowlers do what the Indians did? The first session is an important one, we will find out...

India continue to dominate in this Test series. Yet again their spinners came to the fore and bowled Austtalia out for an average score and their openers got through the nervy period unscathed. Now the Indians will yet again look to bat long and post a big total.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...
Right then! That concludes Day 1! Day 2 promises to be exciting. Join us back for Day 2 at 0930 IST (0400 GMT) and earlier for the build up. Cheers!

Usman Khawaja is up for a chat. He says the pitch is challenging and it is tough to bat. Adds the game plan is the same, he just tried to bat a bit longer. Applauds the performance of Peter Handscomb for the way he played. He says the wicket slightly suits the right-hander. Hopes the pitch does help them on Day 2.

The spinners took 6 wickets but the seamers extracted more, Shami particularly. He didn't start well but was bang on as he proceeded. India could have kept Australia a bit low but got a bit tired. Still, they have done a commendable job. Too early to call, both teams have done a good job on Day 1. Mohammad Shami claimed 4 wickets while Ashwin-Jadeja ended with 6 together.

Australia won the toss and opted to bat first. They off to a watchful start with Usman Khawaja playing a big role. He played a brilliant innings but got no support from other end. Once Peter Handscomb joined, he took on the baton and he played a wonderful innings to keep the innings on track. There was a handful innings from the skipper as well. All in all, Australia manage to get past 250 which is a really good score on this pitch knowing how it was behaving.

A good day of cricket! a good start to the game! Both teams will be happy with how Day 1 went. India will be happy that they end the day without losing any wickets. It is all even as we conclude Day 1.
